question.text:
You are analyzing two real estate investment trusts (REITs) over the last year: REIT X: Total Return = 12%, Dividend Yield = 4% REIT Y: Total Return = 15%, Dividend Yield = 3.5%
Which REIT provided higher capital appreciation over the last year?

answer.text: Both REITs provided the same capital appreciation
Cannot determine from the given data

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook, capital appreciation is the price increase component and dividends are the income component; total return is income plus change in value. So capital appreciation = total return − dividend yield. REIT X: 12% − 4% = 8%. REIT Y: 15% − 3.5% = 11.5%. REIT Y delivered higher capital appreciation. The Trap: Selecting REIT X confuses higher yield with higher appreciation. "Same" or "cannot determine" ignore the data the case provides. Note: Always decompose total return into the income (yield) component and the capital-appreciation (price) component before answering.
